build an rpg and farming simulator: Farming & Animal Husbandry

​Crops: Planting, watering, and harvesting seasonal crops (e.g., strawberries in Spring, blueberries in Summer, pumpkins in Fall).

​Livestock: Raising chickens, ducks, cows, goats, and pigs. Animals produce goods that can be converted into artisan products (like turning milk into cheese or truffles into truffle oil).

​Farm Types: At the start, you choose a farm layout tailored to different playstyles-from classic agricultural plots to riverland fishing spots or wilderness maps with monsters.

​⛏️ Mining & Combat

​The Mines: A 120-floor subterranean system filled with ores (copper, iron, gold, iridium), gemstones, and hostile monsters.

​Combat: Simple real-time sword and weapon combat used to clear floors, gather crafting materials, and discover deeper underground locations like the Skull Cavern.

​🎣 Fishing & Foraging

​Fishing: A skill-based minigame that changes depending on the weather, season, time of day, and water body (ocean, river, mountain lake).

​Foraging: Gathering wild berries, mushrooms, and trees across the map to craft supplies and fences.

​💬 Social Life & Town Dynamics

​Pelican Town: Home to over 30 unique villagers, each with their own schedules, cutscenes, backstories, and personalities.

​Relationships: You can talk to villagers, give them gifts, participate in seasonal town festivals, and even marry one of the 12 eligible bachelors or bachelorettes.

​Roommates & Family: You can build a home, have children with a spouse, or ask Krobus (a friendly shadow monster) to move in as a roommate.

answers.ask: No look was stated - should the valley read as soft storybook countryside, or grounded rustic realism?
answers.answer: Use a soft storybook countryside look, matching the cozy farming RPG tone.

answers.ask: Is the mine a real 120 floors, or a handful of floors that repeat with depth? 120 built floors is a different build entirely.
answers.answer: Make it a real 120-floor mine, as specified, with floors progressing through the stated ore tiers and deeper areas.

answers.ask: Does each player get their own farm, or does one server share a single farm?
answers.answer: Each player gets their own farm so they can choose and develop their selected farm layout independently.

scene_prompt: Create a soft-storybook countryside farming RPG valley with individual player-owned farms, each selectable as a classic agricultural plot, a riverland fishing plot, or a wilderness plot with monster-filled surroundings. Farms contain seasonal crop fields, animal barns and coops for chickens, ducks, cows, goats, and pigs, plus space for a farmhouse, fences, and artisan-production buildings. Connect the farms to a central rural town with over 30 villagers’ homes, shops, festival space, and residential houses. Surround the valley with forageable woods, berry and mushroom patches, and distinct ocean, river, and mountain-lake fishing waters. Include a 120-floor underground mine descending through copper, iron, gold, and iridium tiers, with gemstone chambers, hostile-monster areas, and a deeper cavern region.
blob:
### Genre
Dominant genre: RPG, with Simulation as a secondary genre because the player-owned farm plots support the farming-management loop. The RPG’s `world-hub-dungeon` shape owns the overall valley, town, and mine organization.

### Shape and preset
Use `world-hub-dungeon`, matched from the Action RPG preset: a safe central hub connected to player development areas and a deep combat mine. Retain this preset’s hub-and-dungeon structure, but replace its generic combat focus with the explicitly requested farming valley, individualized farm maps, and 120-floor mine.

### Config requirements
Visible geometry: `safezone-town` is the central rural town, protected and dense with homes, shops, and a festival square; `social-hub` is the compact shop-and-community ring around that square; `hazard-aggro` creates monster-filled wilderness farm surroundings and hostile mine clearings; `collectible-nodes` supplies forage patches and ore/gem chambers; `water-body` provides distinct ocean, river, and mountain-lake shores; `settlement-density` builds the town as a real settlement; `terrain-relief` forms the enclosing valley, wooded slopes, and mountain-lake basin; `npc-population` visibly places over 30 villagers and the named farm animals in their homes, streets, coops, barns, and pens. Invisible layout elements: `spawner-npc` marks hostile-monster origins within wilderness and mine chambers.

### Layout components
Set the town at the valley center as the shared arrival and social zone, with a broad festival green, clustered shops, and over 30 individual villager homes around pedestrian lanes. Place separate player-owned farm maps beyond the town: classic agricultural plots with gridded crop fields, riverland plots organized around fishing banks and channels, and wilderness plots edged by monster territory. Every farm includes a farmhouse site, fenced seasonal fields, animal barns and coops for chickens, ducks, cows, goats, and pigs, artisan-production sheds, and working space between buildings.

Woodland forage belts surround the settlement and farms, with berry patches, mushroom patches, and trees. Put ocean water at one valley edge, a river crossing the farm district, and a mountain lake beneath the high valley slopes. The mine entrance sits outside town and descends through exactly 120 built floors: copper levels first, then iron, gold, and iridium tiers, punctuated by gemstone chambers, hostile areas, and a deeper cavern region. Frame the valley in an elevated three-quarter view, with the town central, farms radiating outward, water readable at separate edges, and the mine’s descending sectional depth implied beside the surface entrance.

### Render order
Use `topdown` first, authoritative because the town-to-farm connections and all 120 mine-floor links must remain navigable; this is not `authored_plan`, since it is neither a maze nor a racing circuit.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is huge, driven by separate player farms, a full town, three fishing-water types, surrounding woods, and 120 distinct mine floors. Theme: soft storybook countryside, cozy rural fantasy, warm seasonal color. Pipeline modifiers: `tiered` for the valley slopes and mountain-lake relief; `P2` for the vertically stacked mine floors; `P3` for the surface-to-underground transition; and `P4` for individual farm maps and the separated mine progression maps.
